days.title: Data Science Overview & Python Setup
days.description: Understand what a data scientist does, set up your development environment, and run your first Python script.
tasks: Install Anaconda or Python 3.10+
Set up VS Code with Python and Jupyter extensions
Understand variables, print statement, and basic syntax
Run your first 'Hello, World!' script
days.exercise: Write a Python script that takes user input for their name and age, and prints a greeting stating the year they will turn 100.

days.title: Basic Data Types & Arithmetic Operations
days.description: Learn about integers, floats, strings, booleans, and how to perform operations on them.
tasks: Study integer and float arithmetic operations
Learn about string concatenation, slicing, and methods
Understand boolean values and comparison operators (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=)
days.exercise: Create variables of different types. Perform arithmetic calculations and string formatting using f-strings.

days.title: Control Flow & Conditional Logic
days.description: Learn to write decisions in Python using if, elif, and else statements, along with logical operators.
tasks: Study if, elif, and else statements
Learn logical operators: and, or, not
Understand nested conditions and ternary operators
days.exercise: Write a program that takes a score (0-100) and prints the letter grade (A, B, C, D, F) based on standard boundaries.

days.title: Loops (For & While)
days.description: Master iteration in Python using loops to execute code blocks repeatedly.
tasks: Learn `for` loops and iteration over ranges
Learn `while` loops and avoid infinite loop traps
Understand control statements: break, continue, pass
days.exercise: Write a script that prints all prime numbers between 1 and 50 using a nested loop.

days.title: Lists & List Comprehensions
days.description: Dive deep into Python's most common sequence type: Lists.
tasks: Understand list creation, indexing, and slicing
Learn list methods: append, extend, insert, remove, pop, sort
Master List Comprehensions for writing clean, efficient code
days.exercise: Given a list of numbers, use a list comprehension to create a new list containing only the squares of the even numbers.

days.title: Dictionaries & Sets
days.description: Explore key-value pairs (dictionaries) and unique collections (sets).
tasks: Learn dictionary syntax, key-value access, and modification
Study dictionary methods: keys(), values(), items(), get(), pop()
Understand sets, set uniqueness, and operations (union, intersection, difference)
days.exercise: Write a program that counts the occurrences of each word in a given paragraph and stores the counts in a dictionary.

days.title: Tuples & Mutability vs Immutability
days.description: Understand tuples and the core concept of mutability in Python data structures.
tasks: Learn tuple creation, indexing, and unpacking
Understand why and when to use tuples instead of lists
Deep dive into mutable vs immutable data types and memory reference
days.exercise: Write a function that returns the minimum, maximum, and average of a list of numbers as a tuple, and unpack them.

days.title: Functions, Scope & Lambda Expressions
days.description: Learn to write reusable code blocks with functions, understand scope, and use anonymous lambda functions.
tasks: Define functions using `def`, parameters, and return statements
Understand Local vs Global scope (LEGB rule)
Write anonymous functions using `lambda`
days.exercise: Create a lambda function that takes a number and returns its square, and a regular function that applies a mathematical formula to a list using custom inputs.

days.title: Error & Exception Handling
days.description: Learn to make your code robust by handling errors and exceptions gracefullly.
tasks: Understand try, except, else, and finally blocks
Learn about common built-in exceptions (ValueError, TypeError, IndexError)
Practice raising custom exceptions using `raise`
days.exercise: Write a function that divides two numbers, catches ZeroDivisionError and TypeError, and prints appropriate error messages.

days.title: File Input / Output (I/O)
days.description: Learn to read and write text files, CSV files, and JSON documents using Python.
tasks: Use the `open()` function and context managers (`with` statement)
Learn to read and write lines to a txt file
Learn to parse and dump JSON using the `json` module

resources.name: Real Python - Reading and Writing Files

days.exercise: Create a JSON file containing student details, read it, update one student's grade, and write the modifications back to the file.

days.title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP): Classes & Objects
days.description: Understand the OOP paradigm in Python, including defining classes, attributes, methods, and instantiation.
tasks: Understand what a class is and how to instantiate objects
Learn about the `__init__` constructor and `self` keyword
Understand instance attributes vs class attributes, and instance methods
days.exercise: Define a `Student` class with attributes name, grades (a list), and a method to calculate their average grade.

days.title: OOP: Inheritance, Polymorphism & Encapsulation
days.description: Deepen your OOP skills by implementing inheritance, polymorphism, and encapsulation (private attributes).
tasks: Implement subclassing (inheritance) and use `super()`
Understand polymorphism by overriding methods
Implement encapsulation using single (_) and double (__) underscores for private attributes
days.exercise: Create a base class `Employee` and a derived class `Manager`. Implement private attributes for salary and methods to calculate bonuses.

days.title: Functional Programming: map, filter, & reduce
days.description: Learn functional programming utilities that make sequence transformations clean and fast.
tasks: Master the `map()` function to apply operations to iterables
Master the `filter()` function to selectively keep elements
Learn `reduce()` from the `functools` module for aggregations
Understand `zip()` and `enumerate()`
days.exercise: Use `filter` and `map` to take a list of strings, filter out those shorter than 5 characters, and convert the remaining strings to uppercase.

days.title: Modules, Packages & Virtual Environments
days.description: Learn how to structure code into files and folders, use pip to install third-party libraries, and manage virtual environments.
tasks: Create a custom module and import it into another file
Learn about virtual environments (`python -m venv` or conda)
Install and manage external libraries using `pip install` and `requirements.txt`
days.exercise: Create a virtual environment, install the `requests` library, write a script to fetch weather/JSON data from a public API, and freeze requirements.

days.title: Phase 1 Review & Coding Challenge
days.description: Consolidate all Phase 1 concepts and solve algorithmic challenges to prepare for Data Science coding assessments.
tasks: Review variables, loops, lists, dicts, OOP, and file I/O
Solve coding challenges on HackerRank/LeetCode (Strings, Arrays, Dicts)
Write clean, documented code following PEP 8 guidelines
days.exercise: Complete a mini-project: Build a simple command-line Contacts Management System using OOP, saving data in JSON.

days.title: Introduction to NumPy & Arrays
days.description: Begin working with NumPy, the core library for numerical computation in Python, and learn about ndarrays.
tasks: Install NumPy and understand its importance in Data Science
Create NumPy arrays from lists and using built-in methods (arange, zeros, ones, linspace)
Understand array attributes: shape, ndim, dtype, size
days.exercise: Create a 3x3 matrix with values ranging from 2 to 10. Check its dimensions, shape, and data type.

days.title: NumPy Indexing, Slicing & Masking
days.description: Learn to retrieve specific elements and subarrays from NumPy arrays using slicing and conditional filters.
tasks: Perform 1D and 2D array indexing and slicing
Understand boolean masking / conditional indexing
Learn about copy vs view in array slicing
days.exercise: Create a 5x5 random integer array. Extract the middle 3x3 submatrix. Filter out and print all values greater than 50.

days.title: Vectorized Operations & Broadcasting
days.description: Understand vectorization, which avoids writing explicit loops, and learning NumPy broadcasting rules.
tasks: Perform element-wise arithmetic operations on arrays
Understand Broadcasting rules (adding vectors of different dimensions)
Learn Universal Functions (ufuncs) like np.sin, np.exp, np.log
days.exercise: Create a 4x3 matrix and a 1x3 vector. Add them together to demonstrate broadcasting, then compute the exponential of the resulting matrix.

days.title: NumPy Mathematical & Statistical Functions
days.description: Learn to calculate descriptive statistics and mathematical values across arrays and specific axes.
tasks: Use sum, mean, median, std, var, min, max on arrays
Understand calculations along specific axes (axis=0 for columns, axis=1 for rows)
Learn indexing functions like argmin, argmax, and where
days.exercise: Create a 4x4 matrix representing exam grades (students as rows, subjects as columns). Find the average score for each subject, and the top-performing student index.

days.title: NumPy Matrix Operations & Linear Algebra
days.description: Master matrix multiplication, transposing, and basic linear algebra functions using NumPy.
tasks: Perform matrix multiplication using `@` or `np.dot`
Transpose matrices and calculate determinants
Solve systems of linear equations using `np.linalg.solve`
days.exercise: Solve the system of equations: 2x + y = 5 and x - 3y = -1 using `np.linalg.solve`.

days.title: Introduction to Pandas: Series & DataFrames
days.description: Step into Pandas, the most important library for data analysis, and learn about its two main structures: Series and DataFrames.
tasks: Understand Pandas Series creation, indexing, and operations
Understand Pandas DataFrames, creating them from dicts, lists, and loading CSVs
View dataset summaries using head(), tail(), info(), describe()
days.exercise: Load a sample CSV file (or create a DataFrame of 10 rows), display its shape, inspect columns, and view basic descriptive statistics.

days.title: Selecting & Filtering Data in DataFrames
days.description: Learn to access specific columns, rows, and slices of data using label and integer-based indexing.
tasks: Master label-based indexing with `.loc[]`
Master index-position indexing with `.iloc[]`
Filter rows based on complex boolean conditions (AND, OR, NOT) and the `.query()` method
days.exercise: From a customer dataset, extract columns 'Name' and 'Spend' for customers who are aged over 30 and have a spend greater than $500.

days.title: Data Cleaning: Missing Values & Duplicates
days.description: Master methods to handle messy real-world datasets, including identifying and repairing missing values and duplicate rows.
tasks: Detect missing values using `.isnull()` and `.sum()`
Impute missing values using `.fillna()` or drop rows/columns using `.dropna()`
Detect and drop duplicates using `.duplicated()` and `.drop_duplicates()`
days.exercise: Load a dataset with missing data. Impute missing numeric values with the column mean, missing categorical values with 'Unknown', and drop duplicate rows.

days.title: Data Transformations & Custom Mapping
days.description: Learn to rename columns, change data types, and apply custom functions to transform DataFrame columns.
tasks: Rename columns using `.rename()` and change types using `.astype()`
Apply custom functions using `.apply()`, `.map()`, and `.applymap()`
Create new columns dynamically based on operations of existing columns
days.exercise: Write a custom function that categorizes income into Low, Medium, and High. Apply this function to create a new column in your DataFrame.

days.title: Data Aggregation & Grouping
days.description: Learn to group rows of data together and compute summary statistics for each group using split-apply-combine.
tasks: Understand the GroupBy mechanism
Compute basic metrics (mean, sum, count) per group
Use `.agg()` to apply multiple custom aggregation functions to different columns
days.exercise: Group a sales dataset by Store and Department, and calculate the average, maximum, and total sales for each department.

days.title: Merging, Joining & Concatenating
days.description: Combine multiple datasets together using SQL-like joins and row/column concatenation.
tasks: Concatenate DataFrames along rows or columns using `pd.concat()`
Merge datasets using `pd.merge()` (Inner, Left, Right, and Outer joins)
Understand merging on single vs multiple keys
days.exercise: Create two DataFrames (Employees and Departments). Merge them using an Inner Join and a Left Join, then compare the outcomes.

days.title: Pivot Tables & Cross-Tabulations
days.description: Reshape your data to perform multidimensional analysis using pivot tables and crosstabs.
tasks: Reshape DataFrames using `.pivot()` and `.pivot_table()`
Compute frequency tables of factors using `pd.crosstab()`
Understand melting / unpivoting data using `pd.melt()`
days.exercise: Create a pivot table showing the average product sales, segmented by Region (rows) and Product Category (columns).

days.title: DateTime Data Handling in Pandas
days.description: Learn to manipulate dates, times, and time-series indexes in Pandas datasets.
tasks: Convert strings to datetime objects using `pd.to_datetime()`
Extract datetime properties (year, month, day, dayofweek)
Perform resample operations (aggregating hourly data to daily or monthly)
days.exercise: Given a dataset of transaction timestamps, extract the month and day name of each transaction, and calculate total sales per weekday.

days.title: String Manipulation in DataFrames
days.description: Learn to clean and manipulate textual data inside Pandas columns using vector string methods.
tasks: Access string accessor `.str`
Perform string cleaning: `.str.lower()`, `.str.strip()`, `.str.replace()`
Extract substrings or check for patterns using regex and `.str.contains()`
days.exercise: Clean a column of messy email addresses: remove trailing whitespaces, convert to lowercase, and filter for rows ending in '@gmail.com'.

days.title: Introduction to Matplotlib
days.description: Begin plotting data visually using Matplotlib, the foundational plotting library in Python.
tasks: Understand Matplotlib's anatomy of a figure
Create simple Line plots, Scatter plots, and Bar charts
Add labels, titles, and legends to your plots
days.exercise: Plot a sine wave using a line plot, and a scatter plot of random coordinates. Customize the color, markers, and line styles.

days.title: Advanced Matplotlib & Subplots
days.description: Learn to construct multi-panel figures and fine-tune plot layouts, ticks, and figure dimensions.
tasks: Create multiple subplots in a single figure using `plt.subplots()`
Customize axes limits, ticks, grid lines, and figure size
Save figures to files using `plt.savefig()`
days.exercise: Generate a 2x2 grid of subplots showing different plot types (line, scatter, bar, histogram) for a dataset and save the figure as a PNG.

days.title: Data Visualization with Seaborn
days.description: Discover Seaborn, a high-level library built on Matplotlib that makes statistical plotting simple and beautiful.
tasks: Understand Seaborn's integration with Pandas DataFrames
Create distribution plots: Histograms, KDE plots, and Box plots
Compare groups using Violin plots and Bar plots
days.exercise: Create a box plot and a violin plot of house prices grouped by the number of bedrooms using a Seaborn dataset.

days.title: Advanced Seaborn: Pairplots, Jointplots & Heatmaps
days.description: Learn to visualize relationships across multiple variables and plot correlation matrices using heatmaps.
tasks: Visualize pairwise relationships in a dataset using `sns.pairplot()`
Analyze bivariate distributions using `sns.jointplot()`
Compute a correlation matrix and visualize it as a heatmap with annotations
days.exercise: Load the Iris dataset. Generate a pairplot colored by Species, and plot a annotated correlation heatmap of the numerical features.

days.title: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA): Part 1
days.description: Perform the first part of an Exploratory Data Analysis: loading data, analyzing shapes, checking for missing values, and summarizing statistics.
tasks: Formulate business questions for a real-world dataset (e.g., Titanic, House Prices)
Load dataset, check data types, shapes, and drop redundant features
Clean missing data and examine categorical value counts
days.exercise: Select a dataset. Write code to inspect columns, print count of nulls, impute missing values, and document your cleaning assumptions.

days.title: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA): Part 2
days.description: Complete your EDA by visualizing data distributions, uncovering patterns, identifying correlations, and drafting findings.
tasks: Plot distributions of target variables and major features
Analyze correlations and relationships between predictors and target variables
Write a markdown summary of key business insights gained from EDA
days.exercise: For the dataset used in Day 34, produce 4 annotated visualizations (distributions, scatter plots, heatmaps) showing significant trends. Write 3 actionable insights.

phases.name: Phase 3: Math & Statistics for Data Science

days.title: Linear Algebra: Vectors & Matrices
days.description: Understand vectors, matrices, dot products, and how they form the mathematical backbone of data representations.
tasks: Learn vector operations: addition, scalar multiplication, dot product
Understand matrix representations, dimensions, and matrix multiplication
Study transposes and symmetric matrices
days.exercise: Manually compute the dot product of two 1D vectors and the product of a 2x3 and 3x2 matrix, then verify in Python.

days.title: Linear Algebra: Determinants & Matrix Inverses
days.description: Learn about singular matrices, matrix determinants, inverses, and solving equations.
tasks: Understand identity matrices and diagonal matrices
Learn how to calculate determinants (for 2x2 and 3x3 matrices) and their geometric meaning
Understand matrix inverses and conditions for invertibility (non-singular matrices)
days.exercise: Calculate the determinant and inverse of a given 2x2 matrix using NumPy. Verify that A multiplied by its inverse equals the Identity matrix.

days.title: Calculus: Limits, Derivatives & Gradients
days.description: Learn how derivatives measure rates of change, which is essential for understanding model optimization.
tasks: Understand the concept of limits and continuous functions
Learn derivative rules (power, product, quotient, chain rules)
Understand partial derivatives and the Gradient vector for multivariate functions
days.exercise: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^2 + 5x - 2, and the gradient of f(x, y) = x^2 * y + y^3 at point (1, 2).

days.title: Optimization: Gradient Descent
days.description: Understand optimization, learning rates, and how models search for global minima.
tasks: Understand cost/loss functions and local vs global minima
Learn the gradient descent update formula: x_new = x_old - learning_rate * gradient
Understand the role of the learning rate and common issues (overshooting, slow convergence)
days.exercise: Implement a simple 1D gradient descent algorithm in Python to find the minimum of f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 4. Start at x=0, set learning rate = 0.1, and run for 20 iterations.

days.title: Descriptive Statistics: Central Tendency & Dispersion
days.description: Learn to summarize a dataset numerically using measures of central tendency and dispersion.
tasks: Study Mean, Median, and Mode (when to use which)
Study Range, Variance, Standard Deviation, and Interquartile Range (IQR)
Understand skewness, kurtosis, and outliers detection using IQR
days.exercise: Given a sample dataset of house prices, compute the mean, median, standard deviation, and identify outliers using the IQR rule (1.5 * IQR).

days.title: Probability Basics & Bayes' Theorem
days.description: Understand core probability concepts, conditional probability, and the famous Bayes' Theorem.
tasks: Define sample space, events, probability axioms
Understand independent and mutually exclusive events
Study Conditional Probability and Bayes' Theorem formula
days.exercise: Solve a conditional probability problem: calculate the probability of a user having a disease given they tested positive, knowing test accuracy and disease base rate (Bayes' Theorem).

days.title: Probability Distributions
days.description: Master probability density functions and study major continuous and discrete distributions.
tasks: Understand Random Variables (discrete vs continuous)
Study Discrete Distributions: Binomial, Poisson
Study Continuous Distributions: Uniform, Normal (Gaussian) and the empirical 68-95-99.7 rule
days.exercise: Use `scipy.stats` to plot a Normal distribution curve. Calculate the probability of a random variable being greater than 1.96 standard deviations from the mean.

days.title: Sampling & The Central Limit Theorem
days.description: Discover why the Normal distribution is ubiquitous in statistics using the Central Limit Theorem (CLT).
tasks: Understand Population vs Sample, sampling bias, and parameters vs statistics
Study the Central Limit Theorem: distribution of sample means
Understand Standard Error of the mean
days.exercise: Write a Python simulation that takes 1000 samples of size n=30 from an exponential distribution, computes their means, and plots a histogram to show that the sample means are normally distributed.

days.title: Confidence Intervals
days.description: Learn to estimate population parameters with ranges of values and associated confidence levels.
tasks: Define Point Estimates and Confidence Intervals
Understand Margin of Error and Critical Values (z-critical, t-critical)
Calculate confidence intervals for population means (known vs unknown variance)
days.exercise: Given a sample of 50 student exam scores, calculate a 95% confidence interval for the population average score in Python using `scipy.stats`.

days.title: Hypothesis Testing Foundations
days.description: Learn the scientific methodology for testing claims, setting hypotheses, and understanding p-values.
tasks: Formulate Null Hypothesis (H0) and Alternative Hypothesis (Ha)
Understand Significance Level (alpha) and p-value decision rules
Distinguish Type I errors (false positive) and Type II errors (false negative)
days.exercise: Write a short summary defining: Null hypothesis, Alternative hypothesis, significance level, p-value, and power of a test.

days.title: Z-Tests & T-Tests
days.description: Learn to run statistical tests to compare sample means using Z-tests and T-tests in Python.
tasks: Learn when to use Z-tests vs T-tests
Perform One-Sample T-test
Perform Independent (Two-Sample) T-test and Paired T-test using `scipy.stats`
days.exercise: Test whether the average height of a sample of 25 plants (mean=15cm, std=3cm) is significantly greater than the historical average of 14cm. Run a 1-sample t-test (alpha=0.05).

days.title: ANOVA & Chi-Square Tests
days.description: Compare means across more than two groups (ANOVA) and analyze categorical variable independence (Chi-Square).
tasks: Understand One-Way ANOVA and post-hoc tests
Learn Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit and Chi-Square Test of Independence
Perform these tests in Python using `scipy.stats` or `statsmodels`
days.exercise: Run a Chi-Square test of independence to determine if customer satisfaction (High, Med, Low) is associated with membership tier (Gold, Silver, Bronze).

days.title: Correlation: Pearson & Spearman
days.description: Study statistical relationships between variables and understand the critical difference between correlation and causation.
tasks: Compute Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient
Compute Spearman rank correlation coefficient for non-linear relationships
Understand confounding variables and why correlation does not imply causation
days.exercise: Calculate the Pearson and Spearman correlations between study hours and exam grades in a small mock dataset. Explain what the coefficients mean.

days.title: Simple Linear Regression (Statistical View)
days.description: Study regression from a statistical standpoint: fit lines, check residuals, and inspect coefficients.
tasks: Understand simple regression formula: y = beta0 + beta1 * x + error
Learn Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) estimation
Inspect residuals, R-squared, and p-values of coefficients using `statsmodels`
days.exercise: Use `statsmodels.api.OLS` to fit a line predicting house price from square footage. Print the summary report and interpret the coefficients and R-squared.

days.title: Phase 3 Review & Case Study
days.description: Consolidate your mathematical and statistical skills by conducting a complete statistical analysis on a dataset.
tasks: Review linear algebra, optimization, probability, and hypothesis testing
Conduct EDA, check distributions, perform outlier removal, run t-tests/chi-square tests, and fit a statsmodels regression line
Document your statistical assumptions and results
days.exercise: Perform a complete statistical case study on an employee churn dataset. Determine if tenure, department, or salary class significantly affects churn (using t-test/chi-square).

days.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
days.description: Understand what machine learning is, classification of algorithms, and the lifecycle of building ML models.
tasks: Learn differences between Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning
Understand the typical pipeline: Ingest -> Clean -> Preprocess -> Feature Engineer -> Train -> Evaluate -> Deploy
Set up Scikit-Learn in your virtual environment
days.exercise: Draw a flowchart of the machine learning pipeline and explain the inputs/outputs of each stage.

days.title: Supervised Learning: Linear & Multiple Regression
days.description: Implement linear regression models with one or more predictor variables using Scikit-Learn.
tasks: Understand regression concepts and coefficients
Fit a `LinearRegression` model using Scikit-Learn
Interpret coefficients and intercept in multiple regression
days.exercise: Train a multiple linear regression model on the Scikit-Learn California housing dataset. Print the weights assigned to each feature.

days.title: Regression Evaluation Metrics
days.description: Learn to measure the performance of your regression models using different metrics.
tasks: Study Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
Study Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and R-squared (Coefficient of Determination)
Understand Adjusted R-squared and residual plotting
days.exercise: Compute the MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R2 score of your California housing regression model on a test split. Plot the residuals vs predicted values.

days.title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff & Under/Overfitting
days.description: Understand the central dilemma of machine learning: balancing bias and variance.
tasks: Define Bias and Variance
Identify overfitting (high variance, low train error, high test error) and underfitting (high bias, high train/test error)
Learn standard ways to prevent overfitting (more data, regularization, model simplification)
days.exercise: Plot a learning curve (training vs validation error across different training set sizes) for a model and diagnose if it has high bias or high variance.

days.title: Regularization: Ridge, Lasso & ElasticNet
days.description: Learn to prevent overfitting in linear models by penalizing large weights using L1 and L2 regularization.
tasks: Understand L2 regularization (Ridge Regression) and its formulation
Understand L1 regularization (Lasso Regression) and its feature-selection properties
Learn ElasticNet (combining L1 and L2) and the penalty weight hyperparameter alpha
days.exercise: Compare performance (coefficients and test set MSE) of Linear, Ridge, and Lasso regression on a dataset with highly correlated features.

days.title: Classification: Logistic Regression
days.description: Learn how logistic regression uses the sigmoid function to map linear outputs to probabilities for classification.
tasks: Understand the Sigmoid function and odds ratios
Study Binary vs Multinomial classification
Fit a `LogisticRegression` model in Scikit-Learn
days.exercise: Train a Logistic Regression model to classify if a patient has diabetes based on diagnostic measurements. Inspect prediction probabilities.

days.title: Classification Evaluation Metrics
days.description: Learn to evaluate classification models using confusion matrices, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC.
tasks: Construct and interpret a Confusion Matrix
Define Accuracy, Precision, Recall (Sensitivity), and F1-score
Understand the precision-recall tradeoff and ROC-AUC curves
days.exercise: For your diabetes classifier, print the classification report (precision, recall, f1) and the confusion matrix. Plot the ROC curve and calculate the AUC score.

days.title: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
days.description: Master KNN, a simple instance-based algorithm used for both classification and regression.
tasks: Understand distance metrics (Euclidean, Manhattan distances)
Learn how the 'K' hyperparameter impacts model boundaries (overfitting vs underfitting)
Implement `KNeighborsClassifier` and scaling requirements
days.exercise: Train a KNN classifier on the Iris dataset. Experiment with different values of K (1, 5, 20) and observe how test accuracy changes.

days.title: Decision Trees
days.description: Learn how decision trees split data using Entropy, Information Gain, or Gini Impurity to make predictions.
tasks: Understand tree splitting criteria (Gini Impurity, Entropy)
Learn tree hyperparameters: max_depth, min_samples_split, min_samples_leaf
Visualize a trained decision tree using `plot_tree`
days.exercise: Train a Decision Tree Classifier, limit `max_depth` to 3, plot the tree diagram, and identify which feature is chosen for the root split.

days.title: Support Vector Machines (SVM)
days.description: Master SVMs, which seek to find optimal separating hyperplanes, and learn about the kernel trick.
tasks: Understand maximal margin classifier and support vectors
Learn soft margins (C hyperparameter)
Understand Kernels (Linear, RBF, Polynomial) for non-linear boundaries
days.exercise: Train SVM models using Linear and RBF kernels on a non-linearly separable dataset. Plot decision boundaries to compare the models.

days.title: Ensemble Learning: Random Forest
days.description: Learn about bagging and implement Random Forests to improve stability and performance over single decision trees.
tasks: Understand Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregating) concept
Learn how Random Forests combine multiple trees with feature bagging
Train `RandomForestClassifier` and extract feature importances
days.exercise: Train a Random Forest model on a dataset. Plot a bar chart showing feature importances to identify which variables are most predictive.

days.title: Ensemble Learning: Gradient Boosting
days.description: Learn about boosting, where trees are trained sequentially to correct previous errors.
tasks: Understand Boosting concept (converting weak learners to strong)
Study AdaBoost (adaptive boosting weight updates)
Study Gradient Boosting (fitting models to residual errors)
days.exercise: Train a `GradientBoostingClassifier` on a dataset. Compare its accuracy and training speed with a Random Forest model.

days.title: Advanced Boosting: XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost
days.description: Explore the industry-standard boosting libraries used in Kaggle and corporate deployments.
tasks: Install and import `xgboost`, `lightgbm`, or `catboost`
Understand why they are faster and often more accurate than standard gradient boosting
Learn about categorical feature handling in CatBoost
days.exercise: Train an XGBoost classifier on a tabular dataset. Tune its learning rate and depth, and measure the accuracy.

days.title: Unsupervised Learning: K-Means Clustering
days.description: Learn to group unlabelled data together using K-Means clustering.
tasks: Understand the K-Means clustering algorithm steps
Determine optimal clusters using the Elbow Method (inertia) and Silhouette Score
Implement `KMeans` in Scikit-Learn
days.exercise: Perform K-Means clustering on a dataset. Plot the Elbow curve for K=1 to 10 and select the optimal number of clusters.

days.title: Hierarchical Clustering & DBSCAN
days.description: Explore alternative clustering algorithms that build hierarchies or group data by density.
tasks: Understand Agglomerative Clustering and Dendrograms
Understand DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering) and core/border/noise points
Learn when to use DBSCAN over K-Means (handling non-spherical clusters)
days.exercise: Apply DBSCAN and K-Means to a concentric-circles dataset. Plot the clusters side-by-side to show why DBSCAN works better on complex geometries.

days.title: Dimensionality Reduction: PCA
days.description: Learn to reduce features, compress information, and visualize high-dimensional datasets using Principal Component Analysis.
tasks: Understand dimensionality reduction and variance explanation
Study the mathematics of Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
Implement `PCA` and interpret the cumulative explained variance ratio
days.exercise: Apply PCA to a dataset with 10+ features. Reduce it to 2 components, plot the components on a scatter plot, and calculate the total variance captured.

days.title: Feature Engineering: Scaling & Encoding
days.description: Prepare your features for models by performing scaling, normalization, and categorical encoding.
tasks: Study Standardization (`StandardScaler`) vs Min-Max Normalization (`MinMaxScaler`)
Encode categorical features using One-Hot Encoding (`OneHotEncoder`) and Label Encoding
Understand data leakage and why scaling must be fit ONLY on training data
days.exercise: Create a dummy DataFrame with text labels and unscaled numbers. Transform the numbers using StandardScaler and encode text using One-Hot Encoding.

days.title: Feature Selection Techniques
days.description: Learn to choose the most informative subset of features to simplify models and speed up training.
tasks: Learn Filter methods (Correlation, Chi-Square, VarianceThreshold)
Learn Wrapper methods (Recursive Feature Elimination - RFE)
Learn Embedded methods (L1 Lasso regularization, Tree-based importances)
days.exercise: Run RFE on a dataset with a RandomForest estimator to select the top 5 most important features.

days.title: Handling Imbalanced Datasets
days.description: Learn to handle class imbalance in classification datasets (e.g., fraud detection).
tasks: Understand the danger of using accuracy on imbalanced data
Learn resampling methods: undersampling, oversampling (SMOTE)
Learn model-level solutions: adjusting decision thresholds and class weights
days.exercise: Using a highly imbalanced mock dataset, apply SMOTE from the `imblearn` library and compare accuracy/F1 metrics before and after resampling.

days.title: Cross-Validation & Hyperparameter Tuning
days.description: Master robust validation techniques and automate hyperparameter search using Grid Search and Randomized Search.
tasks: Understand K-Fold and Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation
Search hyperparameter grids using `GridSearchCV`
Save time on large search spaces using `RandomizedSearchCV`
days.exercise: Use `GridSearchCV` to find the optimal hyperparameters (`n_estimators`, `max_depth`, `min_samples_split`) for a Random Forest classifier.

days.title: Scikit-Learn ML Pipelines
days.description: Assemble data cleaning, feature engineering, and modeling stages into a single robust pipeline to prevent data leakage.
tasks: Understand Scikit-Learn `Pipeline` class
Incorporate preprocessors (`ColumnTransformer`) and classifiers into a pipeline
Fit, predict, and run cross-validation directly on the Pipeline object
days.exercise: Create a Pipeline that takes raw tabular data, imputes missing values, scales numerical features, one-hot encodes categoricals, and applies a Logistic Regression model.

days.title: End-to-End ML Project: Part 1
days.description: Kick off a comprehensive end-to-end Machine Learning project: frame the problem, load the data, conduct detailed EDA, and split the data.
tasks: Select a standard dataset (e.g., Telecom Customer Churn, Employee Attrition)
Write down the business problem statement and success metrics
Perform initial data loading, cleaning, and train-test splits (reserve test set)
days.exercise: Set up your project repository, write a script to load the data, clean it, split it, and write a summary of features.

days.title: End-to-End ML Project: Part 2
days.description: Build pipelines to preprocess training data, engineer new features, train baseline models, and evaluate performances.
tasks: Build a preprocessor using `ColumnTransformer`
Train 3-4 candidate baseline models (e.g., Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost)
Compare cross-validated performance metrics across candidate models
days.exercise: Write a python script that trains multiple models on your processed dataset, compiles cross-validation scores, and produces a comparison box plot.

days.title: End-to-End ML Project: Part 3
days.description: Finalize your ML project: tune the hyperparameters of the best model, evaluate it on the test set, and analyze feature importances.
tasks: Run hyperparameter tuning (Grid/Random Search) on the best performing model from Day 73
Evaluate the final tuned model on the held-out test set to get realistic performance estimates
Extract and plot feature importances/SHAP values and write up recommendations
days.exercise: Write the final evaluation script. Output test classification reports and save your final model to a file using `joblib`.

days.title: Phase 4 Review & ML Interview Prep
days.description: Consolidate ML concepts and practice answering common machine learning theoretical and practical interview questions.
tasks: Review linear vs logistic regression, decision trees, bias-variance, and ensemble algorithms
Practice explaining regularization (L1 vs L2) and evaluation metrics (Precision vs Recall)
Understand how to handle common edge-cases (data drift, missing values, outliers)
days.exercise: Write down clear, concise answers to three common ML interview questions, explaining bias-variance tradeoff, random forests, and F1-score to a layperson.

phases.name: Phase 5: Advanced Topics & Intro to Deep Learning

days.title: Introduction to Deep Learning & ANNs
days.description: Step into Neural Networks: understand artificial neurons, perceptrons, and the feedforward process.
tasks: Understand biological vs artificial neurons
Learn about weight updates, bias, and the linear combination step
Understand the Feedforward neural network architecture (Input, Hidden, Output layers)
days.exercise: Draw the architecture of a 3-layer feedforward network with 4 input nodes, 3 hidden nodes, and 2 output nodes, showing weights.

days.title: Activation Functions & Backpropagation
days.description: Learn how activation functions introduce non-linearity and how backpropagation updates network parameters.
tasks: Study Activation Functions: ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh, Softmax
Understand Cost Functions (Cross-Entropy, MSE)
Learn how Backpropagation uses the chain rule to calculate gradients and update weights
days.exercise: Compute the derivative of the Sigmoid function. Explain why the ReLU function helps solve the vanishing gradient problem.

days.title: Your First Neural Network in TensorFlow/Keras
days.description: Implement and train a simple neural network classifier using TensorFlow/Keras or PyTorch.
tasks: Install `tensorflow` or `torch` in your virtual environment
Define a sequential feedforward network
Compile the model (choose optimizer and loss function) and fit it on a dataset (e.g., MNIST or Iris)
days.exercise: Write a Python script using Keras/PyTorch to train a simple neural network classifier on the MNIST handwritten digits dataset and plot training accuracy/loss curves.

days.title: Preventing Overfitting in Deep Learning
days.description: Learn deep learning regularization techniques, including Dropout, Batch Normalization, and Early Stopping.
tasks: Understand Dropout layers and how they force redundant representations
Learn about Batch Normalization for stabilizing training
Implement Early Stopping based on validation loss curves
days.exercise: Modify your Day 78 script to include a Dropout layer and an EarlyStopping callback. Observe the changes in training epochs.

days.title: Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
days.description: Explore CNNs, the state-of-the-art architecture for processing grids of data like images.
tasks: Understand why fully connected layers fail on large images (parameter explosion)
Learn about Convolutional layers, Filters (kernels), Strides, and Padding
Understand Pooling layers (MaxPooling) and flattening before classification
days.exercise: Build and train a simple CNN in Keras/PyTorch on the CIFAR-10 image dataset. Achieve a test set accuracy of >60%.

days.title: Introduction to Natural Language Processing (NLP)
days.description: Learn standard text preprocessing steps to clean textual data for downstream ML tasks.
tasks: Learn about Tokenization (splitting sentences into words)
Perform Stopword removal, lowercasing, and punctuation cleaning
Understand stemming vs lemmatization (reducing words to root forms) using `nltk` or `spacy`
days.exercise: Using SpaCy or NLTK, take a paragraph of messy text, clean it, tokenize it, remove stopwords, and lemmatize all remaining words.

days.title: Text Representation: Bag of Words & TF-IDF
days.description: Learn to convert text columns into numerical matrices using Bag-of-Words and Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF).
tasks: Understand the Bag-of-Words model and n-grams
Learn the mathematical formula for TF-IDF
Implement `CountVectorizer` and `TfidfVectorizer` in Scikit-Learn
days.exercise: Take a small list of sentences, generate their TF-IDF matrix in Scikit-Learn, and print the words with the highest TF-IDF scores in each document.

days.title: Sentiment Analysis Case Study
days.description: Build an end-to-end NLP classifier that predicts the sentiment of movie or product reviews.
tasks: Load a dataset of text reviews (e.g., IMDB movie reviews)
Preprocess text, build a TF-IDF representation, and split into train/test
Train a Naive Bayes or Logistic Regression classifier and print evaluation metrics
days.exercise: Train a Sentiment Classifier using Naive Bayes. Test the model with 5 custom reviews you write, and inspect the predicted labels.

days.title: Time Series Forecasting Basics
days.description: Understand time-indexed data, trend, seasonality, stationary series, and basic forecasting methods.
tasks: Identify Time Series components: Level, Trend, Seasonality, Noise
Understand Stationarity and why it matters (AdFuller unit root test)
Learn about autoregressive (AR) and moving average (MA) processes (ARIMA basics)
days.exercise: Load a monthly sales dataset, check for stationarity using `statsmodels` adfuller test, perform differencing if needed, and plot the ACF and PACF graphs.

days.title: Phase 5 Review & Advanced Interview Prep
days.description: Consolidate Deep Learning, NLP, and Time Series concepts, and prepare for advanced data science technical interviews.
tasks: Review neural networks, backpropagation, CNN layers, and text vectorization
Practice explaining the math behind TF-IDF and activation functions
Read up on modern Transformer models (BERT, GPT) at a conceptual level
days.exercise: Write down a 2-paragraph explanation of how Transformer attention mechanisms work, suitable for explaining to a junior programmer.

days.title: SQL Basics: Retrieving & Filtering Data
days.description: Master SQL, the primary language for querying databases, and learn to write SELECT queries.
tasks: Understand Relational Databases and SQL syntax
Learn to query columns, filter rows (`WHERE`), and sort results (`ORDER BY`)
Use comparison, logical, and range operators (`IN`, `BETWEEN`, `LIKE`)
days.exercise: Write queries on a mock database (or online sandbox) to select product names with stock < 10, ordered by price descending.

days.title: SQL Aggregations & Grouping
days.description: Learn to summarize database rows, compute group statistics, and filter grouped records using SQL.
tasks: Master aggregation functions: `COUNT()`, `SUM()`, `AVG()`, `MIN()`, `MAX()`
Group rows by unique keys using `GROUP BY`
Filter grouped results using `HAVING` (and understand how it differs from `WHERE`)
days.exercise: Write a query to find the total sales and number of transactions for each store location, keeping only stores with sales > $10,000.

days.title: SQL Joins: Combining Tables
days.description: Learn to write relational queries that combine columns from multiple database tables.
tasks: Learn `INNER JOIN` for matching keys across tables
Learn `LEFT JOIN` and `RIGHT JOIN` for matching keys while keeping unmatched rows
Understand `FULL OUTER JOIN` and `CROSS JOIN`
days.exercise: Write a query that joins a 'Customers' table and an 'Orders' table, returning customer name, order date, and amount, including customers with no orders.

days.title: Advanced SQL: Subqueries, CTEs, & Window Functions
days.description: Learn to write complex analytical queries using subqueries, Common Table Expressions (CTEs), and Window functions.
tasks: Write nested queries (subqueries) in WHERE and FROM clauses
Organize long queries using CTEs (`WITH` keyword)
Perform calculations relative to current rows using Window functions (`ROW_NUMBER()`, `RANK()`, `PARTITION BY`)
days.exercise: Write a query using a CTE and a window function to find the top 3 highest-earning employees in each department.

days.title: Version Control with Git & GitHub
days.description: Master Git, the industry-standard version control system, and learn to collaborate using GitHub.
tasks: Initialize a git repository, check status, stage, and commit changes
Create, check out, and merge branches, and resolve conflicts
Set up a remote repository on GitHub, push local commits, and create Pull Requests (PRs)
days.exercise: Create a new private repository on GitHub, clone it locally, make a change on a branch, merge it locally, and push the main branch to GitHub.

days.title: Building APIs for ML Models: FastAPI
days.description: Learn to write a fast, modern REST API to expose your trained models to other applications.
tasks: Install `fastapi` and `uvicorn` in your virtual environment
Write basic GET and POST endpoints
Understand Pydantic models for request body validation
days.exercise: Create a FastAPI application with a `/health` endpoint that returns API status, and a `/predict` endpoint that takes numerical values and returns a dummy prediction.

days.title: Model Serialization & API Integration
days.description: Serialize your trained machine learning pipelines to disk and load them dynamically in your FastAPI endpoints.
tasks: Serialize Scikit-Learn models using `joblib` or `pickle`
Load model pipelines in the FastAPI startup event handler
Receive user inputs via API, feed them to the model, and return model predictions
days.exercise: Serialize your Day 74 Iris/Diabetes model. Write a FastAPI endpoint that parses inputs, runs predictions using the loaded model, and returns the result.

days.title: Dockerizing Your Data Science Apps
days.description: Learn to write a Dockerfile, package your FastAPI model, and run it inside an isolated container.
tasks: Install Docker on your system
Write a `Dockerfile` specifying base image, copy files, pip install, and CMD
Build the image (`docker build`) and run the container (`docker run` mapping ports)
days.exercise: Write a Dockerfile for your FastAPI prediction app from Day 92. Build the image, run it, and query the container's endpoints using curl.

days.title: Cloud Platforms (AWS/GCP/Azure) Overview
days.description: Learn about the cloud infrastructure offerings and specialized services for training and deploying ML models.
tasks: Understand fundamental cloud concepts (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, serverless)
Study AWS ecosystem for ML (S3 for storage, EC2 for servers, SageMaker for ML)
Study GCP equivalents (Cloud Storage, Compute Engine, Vertex AI)
days.exercise: Write a brief comparative cheat-sheet mapping storage, compute, database, and machine learning services between AWS, GCP, and Azure.

days.title: Phase 6 Review & SQL/Deployment Interview Prep
days.description: Review SQL aggregations, window functions, Git workflows, Docker isolation, and REST API deployment interview questions.
tasks: Practice complex SQL join and aggregation questions
Review Docker containerization benefits, volumes, and ports mapping
Understand continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines
days.exercise: Complete 3 medium-level database problems on LeetCode/HackerRank or write SQL solutions for customer transaction scenarios.

days.title: Capstone Project: Design & Setup
days.description: Choose a substantial capstone project, plan its architecture, set up the repo, and organize data ingestion.
tasks: Select a unique domain (e.g., Credit Card Fraud, Uber Fare Prediction, Airbnb Price Estimator)
Outline the pipeline: Ingestion -> Training -> API -> Docker -> Documentation
Set up GitHub repository and structure directories
days.exercise: Create a one-page design document for your Capstone project, including database structure, model candidates, and deployment options.

days.title: Capstone Project: Model & API Implementation
days.description: Develop features, train the final model, package the pipeline, and expose it via FastAPI endpoints.
tasks: Write preprocessing scripts and train/tune your final model
Implement a FastAPI application that serves this model
Add automated validation scripts to test model boundaries
days.exercise: Write complete training and server code. Ensure your API works locally, responding correctly to invalid inputs.

days.title: Portfolio & GitHub Documentation
days.description: Document your projects on GitHub and present them in a clean, professional manner for hiring managers.
tasks: Write a professional, comprehensive README.md for your Capstone and other major projects
Include architecture diagrams, instructions on running code, and key performance metrics/plots
Clean up repositories: delete draft notebooks, add `.gitignore`, and format code (using black/flake8)

resources.name: How to Write a Great README

days.exercise: Complete a detailed README.md for your Capstone project, adding sections for problem statement, methodology, results, and quickstart.

days.title: Resume Polishing & Portfolio Site Setup
days.description: Format your resume for Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), highlight key projects, and set up a portfolio website.
tasks: Review resumes of successful entry-level data scientists
Structure your resume: projects first, highlighting tools, metrics, and business impact
Create a portfolio site (using GitHub Pages or a single HTML/CSS page) linking your repositories
days.exercise: Refactor your resume or draft one. Highlight 3 projects using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) with quantitative metrics.

days.title: Mock Interviews & Strategy
days.description: Finalize your learning journey by studying interview strategies, behavioral question patterns, and negotiation.
tasks: Practice answering behavioral questions using the STAR method
Prepare questions to ask the interviewers about team structure, tech stack, and roadmap
Develop a daily application strategy: sending personalized notes, leveraging LinkedIn, and networking
days.exercise: Record yourself answering 3 core questions: 'Tell me about yourself', 'Explain a complex project you built', and 'How do you handle messy data?'
